title: GoodWatch title analysis V2 draft 2
description: Proposal only. Registry definitions live in definition.json. Omitted attributes are not assessed.

assessment.description: Integer assessment under the field-specific rubric in definition.json. Zero is not universal absence: centrality zero is no narrative importance; quality/suitability/explicitness/membership use their own anchors.

adrenaline.description: intensity rubric: Excitement and visceral exhilaration during viewing.

tension.description: intensity rubric: Suspense, dread, or anticipation of an uncertain outcome.

fear.description: intensity rubric: Fright or horror experienced, independently of horror genre membership.

perceived_threat.description: intensity rubric: Sense that characters face harm, including harm never shown.

romantic_feeling.description: intensity rubric: Romantic affection or longing evoked in the viewer.

sensuality.description: intensity rubric: Erotic atmosphere or sexual tension, independently of explicit sexual depiction.

warmth.description: intensity rubric: Affectionate, kind, or emotionally welcoming tone.

wholesomeness.description: intensity rubric: Reassurance through care, kindness, and emotional safety.

wonder.description: intensity rubric: Awe, amazement, or fascination with discovery.

pathos.description: intensity rubric: Acute pity, sorrow, or tragic emotional impact.

uncanniness.description: intensity rubric: Unease from the strangely familiar or almost natural.

catharsis.description: intensity rubric: Emotional release after accumulated tension or feeling.

nostalgia.description: intensity rubric: Longing for a remembered or imagined past evoked by the work; not release age.

hopefulness.description: intensity rubric: Optimistic outlook or belief in positive possibilities.

bleakness.description: intensity rubric: Pessimistic, despairing, or nihilistic outlook.

emotional_intensity.description: intensity rubric: Overall strength of emotional engagement, regardless of positive or negative tone.

stress.description: intensity rubric: Sustained pressure, discomfort, or anxiety experienced during viewing.

uplift.description: intensity rubric: Encouragement, joy, or improved spirits evoked.

thought_provocation.description: intensity rubric: Invitation to reflect on ideas, ethics, or interpretations beyond the immediate plot.

playfulness.description: intensity rubric: Light, mischievous, or freely inventive tone.

sentimentality.description: intensity rubric: Overt appeal to tender feelings and emotional attachment.

emotional_restraint.description: intensity rubric: Understated expression and withholding of overt emotional display.

bittersweetness.description: intensity rubric: Positive and painful feelings intertwined rather than merely appearing separately.

absurdity.description: intensity rubric: Experience of incongruity, illogic, or strangeness, whether humorous or unsettling.

escapism.description: intensity rubric: Immersion away from everyday concerns; not limited to fantasy settings.

wish_fulfillment.description: intensity rubric: Invitation to imagine desired powers, relationships, status, or ways of life.

overall.description: intensity rubric: Overall amount and strength of comedy, independently of individual humor styles.

situational.description: intensity rubric: Humor from circumstances, misunderstandings, and complications; no episodic-format requirement.

wit_wordplay.description: intensity rubric: Humor from verbal cleverness, puns, or linguistic ambiguity.

physical.description: intensity rubric: Humor from bodily action, slapstick, or visual physical mishaps.

cringe.description: intensity rubric: Humor from embarrassment or uncomfortable social situations.

absurdist.description: intensity rubric: Humor from nonsense, illogic, or bizarre juxtapositions.

satire.description: intensity rubric: Humorous critique of institutions, behavior, or social conventions.

parody.description: intensity rubric: Humorous imitation of a recognizable work, genre, or style.

dark.description: intensity rubric: Humor about death, suffering, taboo, or tragedy.

running_gags.description: frequency rubric: Recurring jokes whose repetition or variation creates humor.

meta.description: intensity rubric: Humor about storytelling, production, audiences, or the work itself.

deadpan.description: intensity rubric: Humor delivered with apparent seriousness or minimal emotional reaction.

gross_out.description: intensity rubric: Humor relying on bodily fluids, disgust, or vulgar physical material.

crime.description: centrality rubric: Criminal acts and their consequences as subject matter.

mystery.description: centrality rubric: Uncovering an important unknown as a central concern.

war.description: centrality rubric: Armed conflict and its human or societal consequences.

politics.description: centrality rubric: Governance, political institutions, and struggles for political power.

radicalization.description: centrality rubric: A process of adopting increasingly extreme ideological commitments or endorsing extremist action. Distinct from existing political beliefs, ordinary persuasion, rebellion, group secrecy, and coercive group control; those alone do not establish radicalization.

family.description: centrality rubric: Family bonds, conflict, obligations, and belonging.

psychology.description: centrality rubric: Mental processes, internal conflict, or perception as subject matter.

entertainment_industry.description: centrality rubric: The business and practice of entertainment and celebrity.

social_critique.description: centrality rubric: Examination or criticism of social arrangements and norms.

class.description: centrality rubric: Social class, economic inequality, and mobility.

capitalism.description: centrality rubric: Economic systems organized around capital, profit, and ownership.

consumerism.description: centrality rubric: Exploration or critique of acquiring goods, consumption, brands, or possessions as a source of identity, status, or fulfillment. Distinct from capitalism as an economic system; buying or using a product alone is insufficient.

technological_change.description: centrality rubric: Exploration of societal or personal effects of technological development, adoption, or displacement, including effects on work, relationships, institutions, and identity. Gadget presence, advanced technology, or science alone is insufficient.

human_nature.description: centrality rubric: Explicit thematic exploration of what humans are like: capacities, impulses, morality, cooperation, cruelty, or tensions between nature and social conditioning. Ordinary human characters, emotion, or drama alone is insufficient; not a synonym for personal identity, consciousness, or existential meaning.

faith_and_spirituality.description: centrality rubric: Religious belief, spiritual practice, or metaphysical meaning.

business.description: centrality rubric: Commercial organizations, enterprise, and work decisions.

finance.description: centrality rubric: Money management, financial systems, investing, or debt.

environment.description: centrality rubric: Relationships between human activity and ecosystems.

science.description: centrality rubric: Scientific inquiry and its ideas, practice, or consequences.

popular_culture.description: centrality rubric: Popular media, celebrity, fandom, or shared cultural trends.

survival.description: centrality rubric: Meeting essential needs or overcoming threats to continued life.

adventure.description: centrality rubric: Exploration, risk, and discovery outside ordinary life.

hacking.description: centrality rubric: Intrusion into or manipulation of computer systems.

artificial_intelligence.description: centrality rubric: Artificial agents and their interaction with the world.

consciousness.description: centrality rubric: The nature of subjective experience and personhood.

identity.description: centrality rubric: Formation, discovery, concealment, or change of personal identity.

existential_meaning.description: centrality rubric: Purpose, freedom, mortality, and the meaning of existence.

grief.description: centrality rubric: Responses to loss and mourning.

trauma.description: centrality rubric: Lasting effects of overwhelming or harmful experiences.

recovery.description: centrality rubric: Processes of rebuilding after trauma, illness, or crisis.

mental_health.description: centrality rubric: Mental health conditions, care, and lived experience.

addiction.description: centrality rubric: Dependency and its effects on people and relationships.

addiction_recovery.description: centrality rubric: Attempts to overcome dependency and maintain recovery.

trust_and_betrayal.description: centrality rubric: Reliance on others, deception, and broken trust.

coming_of_age.description: centrality rubric: Development toward adult identity, agency, or responsibility.

coming_out.description: centrality rubric: Disclosure or recognition of LGBTQ identity in a social context.

sexuality.description: centrality rubric: Sexual identity, desire, and their social meaning.

gender_identity.description: centrality rubric: Gender identity and its personal or social implications. Distinct from social expectations about gender roles and from sexism; do not infer identity from conformity to or rejection of a role.

gender_roles.description: centrality rubric: Exploration of social expectations, norms, or performances of masculinity, femininity, and gendered roles. Distinct from a person's gender identity and from sexism as discrimination; either may coexist without implying the other.

immigration.description: centrality rubric: Migration across borders and the experience of settlement.

displacement.description: centrality rubric: Loss of home or community through conflict, coercion, or other forces.

gentrification.description: centrality rubric: Neighborhood change associated with investment and displacement.

surveillance.description: centrality rubric: Monitoring, privacy, and control through observation.

disease_and_pandemics.description: centrality rubric: Disease, epidemics, or public-health responses.

climate_change.description: centrality rubric: Climate processes, human causes, or consequences.

inherited_wealth.description: centrality rubric: Inheritance, dynastic wealth, and intergenerational economic advantage.

social_media.description: centrality rubric: Online social platforms and their effects on life.

public_shaming.description: centrality rubric: Public condemnation, reputational punishment, or social exclusion.

justice.description: centrality rubric: Fairness, accountability, punishment, and redress.

guilt.description: centrality rubric: Responsibility, remorse, and moral burden.

forgiveness.description: centrality rubric: Letting go of blame or reconciling after harm.

loyalty.description: centrality rubric: Commitment to people, groups, or principles under pressure.

belonging.description: centrality rubric: Acceptance, community, and finding a place among others.

loneliness.description: centrality rubric: Isolation and unmet desire for connection.

ambition.description: centrality rubric: Pursuit of achievement, status, or recognition.

obsession.description: centrality rubric: Consuming fixation and its consequences.

labor.description: centrality rubric: Working conditions, worker identity, organizing, and exploitation.

colonialism.description: centrality rubric: Colonial domination, resistance, and its legacies.

racism.description: centrality rubric: Racial discrimination and its personal or structural consequences.

sexism.description: centrality rubric: Discrimination or domination based on sex or gender.

caregiving.description: centrality rubric: Responsibility for another person's everyday support and wellbeing.

parenthood.description: centrality rubric: Becoming or being a parent and its consequences.

aging.description: centrality rubric: Later life, changing capacities, and social experiences of aging.

midlife.description: centrality rubric: Reassessment and transitions in middle adulthood.

retirement.description: centrality rubric: Leaving paid work and adjusting to life afterward.

early_adulthood.description: centrality rubric: Independence, work, and relationships in early adult life.

education.description: centrality rubric: Learning, schooling, and educational institutions.

artistic_creation.description: centrality rubric: Making art and the motivations or struggles involved.

action.description: membership rubric: Genre identity organized substantially around physical action and conflict.

adventure.description: membership rubric: Genre identity organized around journeys, exploration, and peril.

comedy.description: membership rubric: Genre identity organized around humor.

drama.description: membership rubric: Genre identity organized around sustained human conflict and emotional development.

thriller.description: membership rubric: Genre identity organized around suspense, danger, and escalating uncertainty.

horror.description: membership rubric: Genre identity organized around fear, dread, or horror.

science_fiction.description: membership rubric: Genre identity involving speculative science, technology, or societies.

fantasy.description: membership rubric: Genre identity involving supernatural or magical premises.

romance.description: membership rubric: Genre identity centered on a romantic relationship and its development.

mystery.description: membership rubric: Genre identity centered on uncovering an unknown or solving a puzzle.

crime.description: membership rubric: Genre identity centered on crime, criminals, or criminal investigation.

western.description: membership rubric: Genre identity drawing on frontier-western conventions.

neo_western.description: membership rubric: Western conventions adapted to a modern setting.

giallo.description: membership rubric: Genre identity drawing on stylized Italian mystery-thriller and horror conventions.

kaiju.description: membership rubric: Genre identity centered on giant monsters and their impact.

disaster.description: membership rubric: Genre identity organized around a major catastrophe.

superhero.description: membership rubric: Genre identity drawing on superhero narrative conventions; powers alone do not establish membership.

zombie.description: membership rubric: Genre identity organized around zombies or zombie-like contagion.

slasher.description: membership rubric: Horror genre identity organized around a killer stalking and attacking victims.

creature_feature.description: membership rubric: Genre identity organized around encounters with threatening creatures.

neo_noir.description: membership rubric: Modern use of noir conventions such as fatalism, moral ambiguity, and criminal intrigue.

space_western.description: membership rubric: Combination of western conventions and a spacefaring setting.

sword_and_sorcery.description: membership rubric: Fantasy adventure organized around personal peril, swordplay, and sorcery.

cozy_mystery.description: membership rubric: Mystery conventions with a reassuring social setting and limited graphic menace.

romantic_comedy.description: membership rubric: Romance and comedy jointly organize the work.

melodrama.description: membership rubric: Genre mode built around heightened emotional conflict and expressive plotting.

musical.description: membership rubric: Genre identity in which musical performance is integral to storytelling.

war.description: membership rubric: Genre identity substantially organized around warfare.

historical_drama.description: membership rubric: Dramatic genre identity grounded in a past historical setting.

biographical.description: membership rubric: Genre identity organized around the life of a real person.

true_crime.description: membership rubric: Factual treatment of actual crime; fictional crime is insufficient.

psychological_thriller.description: membership rubric: Thriller conventions organized around perception, manipulation, or mental conflict.

conspiracy_thriller.description: membership rubric: Thriller conventions organized around concealed coordination and institutional danger.

survival_thriller.description: membership rubric: Thriller conventions organized around immediate survival under sustained threat.

legal_thriller.description: membership rubric: Thriller conventions organized around legal conflict and proceedings.

police_procedural.description: membership rubric: Crime conventions emphasizing investigative procedure and institutional police work.

gangster.description: membership rubric: Crime conventions emphasizing organized criminal groups and their internal lives.

whodunit.description: membership rubric: Mystery conventions organized around identifying who committed a crime.

puzzle_box.description: membership rubric: Mystery conventions inviting reconstruction of deliberately concealed narrative rules or structure.

space_opera.description: membership rubric: Science-fiction conventions emphasizing large-scale space adventure and heightened conflict.

epic_fantasy.description: membership rubric: Fantasy conventions emphasizing expansive worlds, large stakes, and extended quests or conflicts.

urban_fantasy.description: membership rubric: Fantasy conventions combined with a recognizably urban, usually modern social environment.

dark_fantasy.description: membership rubric: Fantasy conventions combined with a threatening or macabre horror-inflected atmosphere.

investigation.description: centrality rubric: Characters gather evidence to explain an event or identify responsibility.

pursuit.description: centrality rubric: An extended chase or hunt organizes the story.

rescue.description: centrality rubric: Saving someone from captivity or danger organizes the story.

escape.description: centrality rubric: Getting out of confinement or an unsafe situation organizes the story.

quest.description: centrality rubric: A journey toward a defined objective organizes the story.

competition.description: centrality rubric: A contest with rivals and an outcome organizes the story.

relationship_development.description: centrality rubric: Changes in a relationship organize the story.

everyday_life.description: centrality rubric: Ordinary routines and small events organize the story.

survival.description: centrality rubric: Remaining alive under threatening conditions organizes the story.

heist.description: centrality rubric: Planning, carrying out, or dealing with a theft organizes the story.

espionage.description: centrality rubric: Secret intelligence gathering or covert state operations organize the story.

military_operation.description: centrality rubric: An organized military mission structures the story.

legal_case.description: centrality rubric: Legal proceedings or preparation for them structure the story.

political_struggle.description: centrality rubric: Pursuit or exercise of political power structures the story.

underdog_rise.description: centrality rubric: An initially disadvantaged character gains standing or succeeds against stronger opposition.

revenge.description: centrality rubric: Retaliation for a perceived wrong drives an arc.

vigilantism.description: centrality rubric: Characters enforce their own justice outside formal authority.

rags_to_riches.description: centrality rubric: A character moves from poverty to substantial wealth.

fall_from_grace.description: centrality rubric: A character loses status, reputation, or moral standing.

redemption.description: centrality rubric: A character attempts to make amends or change after wrongdoing.

mistaken_identity.description: centrality rubric: A character is consequentially taken to be someone else.

memory_loss.description: centrality rubric: Consequential lost or inaccessible memories, missing periods of time, or inability to recall one's own actions. Includes such gaps without a clinical amnesia diagnosis; does not require permanent loss. Ordinary forgetfulness and information withheld only from the audience are insufficient.

body_swap.description: centrality rubric: Characters exchange bodies or consciousness across bodies.

fish_out_of_water.description: centrality rubric: An unfamiliar social or physical environment challenges a character.

secret_identity.description: centrality rubric: Concealing an identity or maintaining a double life drives the story.

road_trip.description: centrality rubric: An overland journey with encounters along the way structures the story.

tournament.description: centrality rubric: A sequence of competitive rounds structures an arc.

training.description: centrality rubric: Learning or practice builds abilities toward a later challenge.

race_against_time.description: centrality rubric: A consequential deadline structures the conflict.

single_night.description: centrality rubric: The main action is concentrated in one eventful night.

locked_room.description: centrality rubric: An apparently inaccessible crime scene creates the central puzzle.

conspiracy.description: centrality rubric: Hidden coordination among powerful actors drives the plot.

apocalypse_survival.description: centrality rubric: Surviving societal collapse or a world-ending event drives the plot.

haunted_house.description: centrality rubric: An inhabited or visited dwelling is the focal site of a haunting.

chosen_one.description: centrality rubric: A character is singled out for a special, consequential role.

prophecy.description: centrality rubric: Predictions of destiny shape choices and events.

macguffin_quest.description: centrality rubric: Pursuit of an object whose plot function exceeds its intrinsic characterization.

final_survivor.description: centrality rubric: A surviving focal character confronts a threat after others are eliminated.

apparent_death.description: centrality rubric: A character appears to die but is later revealed to be alive.

mentor_death.description: centrality rubric: A mentor dies and the death matters to the mentee's arc.

doppelganger.description: centrality rubric: A double or lookalike produces meaningful events, identity confusion, recurring humor, or conflict. Antagonism or conflict is not required. Incidental resemblance without a narrative use is insufficient.

hidden_antagonist_reveal.description: centrality rubric: A character's antagonistic role is concealed and later revealed.

romantic_development.description: centrality rubric: Formation or deepening of a romantic relationship matters to the story.

established_couple.description: centrality rubric: An existing romantic partnership matters to the story.

marriage.description: centrality rubric: Marriage and its obligations or conflicts matter to the story.

breakup_or_divorce.description: centrality rubric: Ending a partnership matters to the story.

partner_bereavement.description: centrality rubric: Loss of a romantic partner matters to the story.

love_triangle.description: centrality rubric: Competing romantic attachments among three people matter to the story.

enemies_to_lovers.description: centrality rubric: An antagonistic relationship develops into romance.

forbidden_romance.description: centrality rubric: A romantic relationship faces a consequential social or institutional prohibition.

slow_burn_romance.description: centrality rubric: Romantic development unfolds gradually through delayed intimacy or commitment.

queer_romance.description: centrality rubric: An explicitly depicted LGBTQ romantic relationship matters to the story.

workplace_romance.description: centrality rubric: A romantic relationship between coworkers matters to the story.

age_gap_romance.description: centrality rubric: A substantial age difference is consequential to a romantic relationship.

friendship.description: centrality rubric: Non-romantic bonds of friendship matter to the story.

male_friendship.description: centrality rubric: Friendship among men matters to the story.

female_friendship.description: centrality rubric: Friendship among women matters to the story.

mentor_mentee.description: centrality rubric: Guidance and learning between mentor and mentee matter to the story.

student_teacher.description: centrality rubric: A formal educational student-teacher relationship matters to the story; no romantic implication.

rivalry.description: centrality rubric: Competition or mutual opposition between characters matters to the story.

forced_proximity.description: centrality rubric: Circumstances oblige characters to remain close or share space.

adversaries_cooperate.description: centrality rubric: Opposing characters must work together.

found_family.description: centrality rubric: Chosen bonds serve a family-like role in the story.

family_conflict.description: centrality rubric: Sustained conflict or harmful dysfunction within a family matters to the story.

intergenerational.description: centrality rubric: Relationships across generations matter to the story.

generational_trauma.description: centrality rubric: Trauma transmitted or repeated across generations matters to the story.

parent_child.description: centrality rubric: The relationship between parent and child matters to the story.

siblings.description: centrality rubric: Sibling relationships matter to the story.

caregiver_dependent.description: centrality rubric: Care and dependence between characters matter to the story.

human_animal_companionship.description: centrality rubric: An emotional bond between a person and animal matters to the story.

coercive_relationship.description: centrality rubric: Manipulation, coercion, or control within an interpersonal relationship matters to the story. Systematic control of members by a group is assessed separately as coercive_group_control; neither automatically implies the other.

coercive_group_control.description: centrality rubric: A group or leader systematically controls members through intimidation, isolation, dependency, punishment, or suppression of autonomy. Distinct from interpersonal coercion, voluntary discipline, secrecy, and radicalization; any of these may coexist but does not imply group control.

ensemble.description: centrality rubric: Several focal characters share narrative attention and agency.

antihero.description: centrality rubric: A focal character departs substantially from conventional heroic ethics or behavior.

morally_ambiguous_cast.description: centrality rubric: Moral ambiguity among multiple major characters matters to the work.

transformation_arc.description: centrality rubric: Substantial change in a focal character's beliefs, identity, or behavior.

intellectual_problem_solver.description: centrality rubric: A focal character's reasoning or specialized intellectual ability drives events.

detective_lead.description: centrality rubric: A focal character acts as an investigator or detective.

female_protagonist.description: centrality rubric: A woman or girl occupies a protagonist role, independently of competence or characterization quality.

child_protagonist.description: centrality rubric: A child occupies a protagonist role.

teen_protagonist.description: centrality rubric: A teenager occupies a protagonist role.

older_adult_protagonist.description: centrality rubric: An older adult occupies a protagonist role.

child_agency.description: centrality rubric: Children make consequential choices that affect events.

female_character_agency.description: centrality rubric: Women or girls make consequential choices that affect events.

workplace_team.description: centrality rubric: A team formed through work is a central social unit.

family_business.description: centrality rubric: A family-run business is a central social unit.

unaccompanied_children.description: centrality rubric: Children without their usual caregivers form a central social situation.

teen_peer_group.description: centrality rubric: Teenage friendships and peer-group dynamics form a central social situation.

clandestine_groups.description: centrality rubric: A secret society or organized group whose membership, meetings, activities, or aims are deliberately concealed. Secrecy is the defining feature, not coercion or extremist ideology; a secret held by one person, an ordinary private friendship, or crime alone is insufficient.

lgbtq_characters.description: centrality rubric: Explicitly established LGBTQ characters have narrative importance; do not infer from allegory or creator identity.

neurodivergent_characters.description: centrality rubric: Explicitly established neurodivergent characters have narrative importance; do not diagnose from behavior.

disabled_characters.description: centrality rubric: Explicitly established disabled characters have narrative importance.

immigrant_characters.description: centrality rubric: Explicitly established immigrant characters have narrative importance.

advanced_technology.description: centrality rubric: Technology substantially beyond the work's contemporary baseline shapes its world.

magic.description: centrality rubric: Supernatural abilities or forces understood as magic shape the world.

simulation.description: centrality rubric: An artificial simulation is an important layer of reality.

virtual_reality.description: centrality rubric: Characters experience an interactive digitally mediated environment.

parallel_worlds.description: centrality rubric: Coexisting alternative realities matter to the world.

time_travel.description: centrality rubric: Movement across time outside ordinary chronological passage matters to the world.

travel_to_past.description: centrality rubric: Travel to an earlier time matters to the world.

travel_to_future.description: centrality rubric: Travel to a later time matters to the world.

time_loop.description: centrality rubric: Repetition of a period of time matters to the world or narrative.

dystopian_society.description: centrality rubric: Oppressive or deeply dysfunctional social arrangements define the world.

post_apocalyptic.description: centrality rubric: Life after a civilization-scale catastrophe defines the world.

spacefaring.description: centrality rubric: Travel or life beyond Earth is consequential to the world.

robots.description: centrality rubric: Embodied artificial machines functioning as agents matter to the world; not synonymous with AI.

myth_and_folklore.description: centrality rubric: Recognizable mythological or folkloric traditions shape the world.

scientific_rigor.description: intensity rubric: Attention to scientific constraints and explanatory consistency; not an inverse of speculative freedom.

speculative_freedom.description: intensity rubric: Freedom to use speculative premises without scientific elaboration.

worldbuilding_depth.description: intensity rubric: Detail and interconnection in the world's institutions, history, and rules.

lore_dependence.description: intensity rubric: Importance of remembering mythology or lore to follow the work.

magic_rule_detail.description: intensity rubric: Elaboration of rules and constraints governing magic.

everyday_realism.description: intensity rubric: Attention to plausible ordinary behavior and material conditions, independently of era.

urban.description: centrality rubric: A city environment is narratively important.

small_town.description: centrality rubric: A small town environment is narratively important.

rural.description: centrality rubric: A countryside or village environment is narratively important.

frontier.description: centrality rubric: A frontier environment is narratively important.

polar.description: centrality rubric: An Arctic, Antarctic, or comparable polar environment is narratively important.

mountains.description: centrality rubric: Mountain landscapes are narratively important.

forest.description: centrality rubric: Woodland environments are narratively important.

desert.description: centrality rubric: Desert environments are narratively important.

ocean.description: centrality rubric: Open sea or marine environments are narratively important.

island.description: centrality rubric: Island environments are narratively important.

space_station.description: centrality rubric: An orbital or deep-space station is narratively important.

spacecraft.description: centrality rubric: A vehicle traveling through space is narratively important.

underground.description: centrality rubric: Underground spaces are narratively important.

bunker.description: centrality rubric: A protective or military bunker is narratively important.

mansion.description: centrality rubric: A large private residence or estate is narratively important.

home.description: centrality rubric: Domestic living spaces are narratively important.

school.description: centrality rubric: A primary or secondary school is narratively important.

university.description: centrality rubric: A university or college environment is narratively important.

office.description: centrality rubric: An office workplace is narratively important.

hospital.description: centrality rubric: A hospital or clinic is narratively important.

restaurant.description: centrality rubric: A restaurant or cafe is narratively important.

bar_or_club.description: centrality rubric: A bar, nightclub, or similar nightlife venue is narratively important.

hotel.description: centrality rubric: A hotel or resort is narratively important.

factory.description: centrality rubric: An industrial production site is narratively important.

laboratory.description: centrality rubric: A research or testing laboratory is narratively important.

prison.description: centrality rubric: A prison or detention facility is narratively important.

salon.description: centrality rubric: A beauty or hair salon is narratively important.

subway.description: centrality rubric: An underground urban rail system is narratively important.

airport.description: centrality rubric: An airport is narratively important.

amusement_park.description: centrality rubric: An amusement park is narratively important.

circus.description: centrality rubric: A circus or carnival is narratively important.

theater.description: centrality rubric: A theater or performance stage is narratively important.

museum.description: centrality rubric: A museum or gallery is narratively important.

library_or_bookshop.description: centrality rubric: A library or bookshop is narratively important.

religious_site.description: centrality rubric: A place of worship or religious practice is narratively important.

cemetery.description: centrality rubric: A cemetery or burial ground is narratively important.

engineering.description: centrality rubric: Engineering work matters to the story.

computing.description: centrality rubric: Computing and information-technology work matter to the story.

healthcare.description: centrality rubric: Healthcare work matters to the story.

policing.description: centrality rubric: Police work matters to the story; separate from military work.

military.description: centrality rubric: Military service matters to the story.

law.description: centrality rubric: Legal professional work matters to the story.

business.description: centrality rubric: Business management or entrepreneurship matters to the story.

finance.description: centrality rubric: Financial professional work matters to the story.

service.description: centrality rubric: Hospitality, retail, or other service work matters to the story.

arts.description: centrality rubric: Artistic or entertainment work matters to the story.

education.description: centrality rubric: Teaching or academic work matters to the story.

journalism.description: centrality rubric: Reporting and news production matter to the story.

organized_crime.description: centrality rubric: Work within organized criminal enterprises matters to the story.

piracy.description: centrality rubric: Maritime piracy as an occupation or way of life matters to the story.

cooking.description: centrality rubric: Preparing food matters to the story; includes professional and domestic contexts.

baking.description: centrality rubric: Baking matters to the story as a specific culinary activity.

dining.description: centrality rubric: Eating out and food experiences matter to the story.

travel.description: centrality rubric: Travel and encounters away from home matter to the story.

tropes.memory_loss.description: Lost or inaccessible memories or missing periods of a character's own experience occur, whether or not diagnosed as amnesia. Ordinary forgetfulness or withholding information only from the audience is insufficient.

relationships.coercive_group_control.description: A group or leader systematically controls members through intimidation, isolation, dependency, punishment, or suppression of autonomy. Distinct from interpersonal coercion, voluntary discipline, secrecy, and radicalization; any of these may coexist but does not imply group control.

characters.clandestine_groups.description: A secret society or organized group whose membership, meetings, activities, or aims are deliberately concealed. Secrecy is the defining feature, not coercion or extremist ideology; a secret held by one person, an ordinary private friendship, or crime alone is insufficient.
